title: Shrinking inequivalent smooth models to glue them separatedly
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer $\pi$, fraction field $E$, residue field $k$, and $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Products and fibres are scheme-theoretic base changes [def-pc-base-change]. Smooth and finite type have the meanings of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Write $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ for a strict henselization at a geometric closed point and $E^{\mathrm{sh}}=\operatorname{Frac}(R^{\mathrm{sh}})$ [def-weil-geometric-point, def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. An open in a scheme over a trait is base-dense if it is dense in each fibre. A rational map over that trait is a morphism on a base-dense open, modulo agreement on a base-dense common open; its domain of definition is the union of all representative domains. A birational map over the trait is an isomorphism between base-dense opens. For a smooth separated finite-type $E$-scheme $X$, a smooth model means a smooth separated finite-type $T$-scheme $M$ with a specified identification $M_E\simeq X$. Let $X/E$ be a nonempty smooth separated finite-type scheme, and let $M_1,\ldots,M_r$, $r\geq1$, be smooth models of $X$ with nonempty irreducible special fibres. Suppose that for distinct $i,j$ there is no $T$-rational map $M_i\dashrightarrow M_j$ inducing the identity of $X$ (and likewise with $i,j$ interchanged). Then there are opens $V_i\subseteq M_i$, containing the entire generic fibre and the generic point of $(M_i)_k$, such that for $i\ne j$ the diagonal copy of $X$ is closed in $V_i\times_TV_j$. Gluing these $V_i$ along their identified generic fibres gives a smooth separated finite-type $T$-scheme $Y$ with $Y_E\simeq X$ and $Y_k=\coprod_i(V_i)_k$. Each $V_i\to Y$ is an open immersion and the $V_i$ cover $Y$.

source.place: 4.3 Proposition 4, first two proof paragraphs, printed pp.106-107 (PDF pp.112-113): schematic closures of cross diagonals, shrinking their nowhere-dense special images, and gluing. Primary scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf; local literature copy WANTED.

proof.text: The DVR $R$ is Noetherian since its ideals are principal. Its primes are $(0)$ and $(\pi)$, and its localizations are the field $E$ and $R$; its dimension is one, so $R$ is regular. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization] it is a regular ring. Using the smooth-ring-map description in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-smooth-ascent] makes every smooth affine chart of each $M_i$ regular. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-normal] their local rings are domains, so each $M_i$ is reduced. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] the $M_i$ and their products over $T$ are Noetherian; the product maps are of finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. Each has finitely many irreducible components by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-components]. By [lem-pc-smooth-flat] each $M_i/T$ is flat and locally finitely presented. No connectedness or irreducibility of the entire generic fibre is asserted.

Write $\xi_i$ for the generic point of $(M_i)_k$. This special fibre is reduced by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced], and is nonempty and irreducible by hypothesis, hence integral. Its local ring at $\xi_i$ is a field by [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field]. For $A_i=\mathcal O_{M_i,\xi_i}$, [lem-sbc-scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient] identifies $A_i/\pi A_i$ with that field. Thus the maximal ideal of $A_i$ is $(\pi)$. The local flatness of $M_i/T$, with [lem-trf-flat-module-torsionfree-domain], makes multiplication by $\pi$ injective, so $\pi\ne0$ in $A_i$. Step 1 makes $A_i$ a Noetherian local domain. The principal-maximal-ideal characterization in [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] now proves that $A_i$ is a DVR with uniformizer $\pi$.

source.place: Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), principal nonzero maximal ideal criterion; schemes.tex fibre stalk quotient; BLR 4.3 Proposition 4, printed p.106, local ring at the special generic point.

proof.text: Fix $i\ne j$. In $P_{ij}=M_i\times_T M_j$, let $\Gamma_{ij}$ be the scheme-theoretic image of $\delta_{ij}:X\longrightarrow P_{ij}$, the two generic-fibre identifications on its projections. The generic fibre of $P_{ij}$ is open (it is $D(\pi)$), and $\delta_{ij}$ is a closed immersion into that open because $X/E$ is separated. This map is quasi-compact and quasi-separated: locally its source is a closed subscheme of an open in the Noetherian target; the open immersion is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-noetherian-open-immersion-qc]. By [lem-trf-reduced-scheme-image], $\Gamma_{ij}$ is reduced with support the closure of the diagonal. By [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-restrict-open], its restriction to the generic fibre is exactly $\delta_{ij}(X)$. Its projections $p_i:\Gamma_{ij}\to M_i$, $p_j:\Gamma_{ij}\to M_j$ are finite type: their closed inclusion is finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], and product projection and composition preserve finite type. Both generic projections are the specified isomorphisms with $X$.

source.place: Tag 056B (lemma-scheme-theoretic-image-reduced), Tag 01R8 (lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image); BLR 4.3 Proposition 4, printed p.106, schematic closure of the cross diagonal.

proof.text: Suppose $y\in\Gamma_{ij}$ satisfies $p_i(y)=\xi_i$. By [lem-sfb-noetherian-injective-germ-neighbourhood], choose an affine neighbourhood $U$ of $\xi_i$ in $M_i$ whose coordinate ring embeds into $A_i$. It is a domain, so $U$ is integral by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field]. Its open $U_E$ is nonempty: $\pi$ is nonzero in this domain. Restricting the scheme-theoretic image to $U\times_T M_j$, by [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-restrict-open], identifies $p_i^{-1}(U)$ with the reduced closure of the graph on $U_E$. Since $U_E$ is integral, this closure is irreducible and reduced, hence integral. The open graph on $U_E$ has the same function field as $U$, and $p_i$ induces the identity of these fields. By [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field], the local map $A_i\to B=\mathcal O_{\Gamma_{ij},y}$ therefore embeds both into the same field $L=\operatorname{Frac}(A_i)$, as subrings, and the inclusion is local. This argument uses only an integral neighbourhood of $\xi_i$; other generic components of $X$ cause no difficulty.

source.place: Tag 0BX3 (lemma-ring-affine-open-injective-local-ring), case (2); morphisms.tex Tag 056B; BLR 4.3 Proposition 4, printed p.106, comparison of the two local rings.

proof.text: In Step 4 the inclusion $A_i\subseteq B\subseteq L$ is equality. Indeed each nonzero $b\in L$ has the form $u\pi^m$ with $u\in A_i^\times$ and $m\in\mathbf Z$. If $b\in B$ had $m<0$, then $u^{-1}b\pi^{-m-1}=\pi^{-1}\in B$, contradicting that the local map sends $\pi\in\mathfrak m_{A_i}$ into $\mathfrak m_B$. Thus every element of $B$ lies in $A_i$. Apply [lem-trf-finite-type-stalk-isomorphism-open-neighbourhood] to $p_i$: its target $M_i$ is reduced with finitely many irreducible components by Step 1, and it is finite type by Step 3. There is an open $W$ of $y$ on which $p_i$ is an open immersion onto an open $U'$ containing $\xi_i$. The map $p_j\circ(p_i|_W)^{-1}:U'\to M_j$ agrees with the generic identity wherever defined. Glue it with the identity $X=(M_i)_E\to(M_j)_E$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. The resulting domain $U'\cup(M_i)_E$ is base-dense, since it contains the entire generic fibre and $\xi_i$. This is a forbidden $T$-rational identity map. Hence $\xi_i\notin p_i(|(\Gamma_{ij})_k|)$. The same argument for the reversed ordered pair excludes $\xi_j$ from the other projected image.

source.place: Tag 00PD, valuation description of a DVR; varieties.tex Tag 09NH (lemma-local-isomorphism); BLR 4.3 Proposition 4, printed pp.106-107, contradiction from a rational identity map.

proof.text: Put $C_{ij}=p_i(|(\Gamma_{ij})_k|)\subseteq |(M_i)_k|$. The fibre map $(\Gamma_{ij})_k\to(M_i)_k$ is finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. Its target is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], and its local finite-type hypothesis therefore gives local finite presentation by [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth]. Its target is qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine], since it is separated finite type over $k$ (its diagonal is the base change of that of $M_i/T$). Chevalley's theorem [lem-weil-pbc-chevalley-constructible-image] applied to the whole source makes $C_{ij}$ constructible. Step 5 says that it omits the generic point $\xi_i$.

source.place: Tag 054J (lemma-chevalley), Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian), Tag 01TU (lemma-locally-finite-type-finite-presentation); BLR 4.3 Proposition 4, printed p.106, nowhere dense special images.

proof.text:
The closure $F_{ij}=\overline{C_{ij}}$ inside $(M_i)_k$ is proper. To see this directly, write $C_{ij}$ as a finite union of locally closed sets $O_a\cap Z_a$ with $O_a$ open and $Z_a$ closed, using [def-weil-constructible-subset]. If its closure were the irreducible space $(M_i)_k$, one of these finitely many pieces would have full closure. Then $Z_a=(M_i)_k$ and $O_a$ is nonempty, so that piece contains $\xi_i$, contrary to Step 5. Since the special fibre is closed in $M_i$, each $F_{ij}$ is closed in $M_i$. Set
$$V_i=M_i\setminus\bigcup_{j\ne i}F_{ij}.$$
The union is finite and omits $\xi_i$; the $V_i$ contain their special generic points and the entire generic fibre. For $r=1$ the union is empty and $V_1=M_1$.

source.place: Topology Tags 005G (definition-constructible), 005L (lemma-constructible-noetherian); elementary finite-union argument in BLR 4.3 Proposition 4, printed p.106.

proof.text: For $i\ne j$, restrict the closed subscheme $\Gamma_{ij}\subseteq M_i\times_T M_j$ to $V_i\times_T V_j$. Its special fibre is empty: a special point would project into $C_{ij}$ and also into $V_i$, whereas $C_{ij}\subseteq F_{ij}$ was removed. Consequently this restricted scheme factors through the open generic fibre of the product: an open restriction whose inverse-image complement has no points is the entire scheme. There it is exactly the diagonal copy of $X$ by Step 3. Thus the morphism $X\to V_i\times_T V_j$ is a closed immersion, not merely a map with closed point image: it is the restriction of the closed immersion of $\Gamma_{ij}$, as guaranteed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. This supplies the asserted scheme structure on the cross diagonal.

source.place: BLR 4.3 Proposition 4, printed p.106, condition (*); Stacks schemes.tex Tag 01JU (lemma-base-change-immersion), closed-immersion case.

proof.text: Use gluing data with charts $V_i$, overlap $V_i$ for equal indices, and overlap $X$ for distinct indices, with all transition maps induced by the specified identifications $(V_i)_E\simeq X$. The inverse and cocycle identities hold because each transition is the identity in the common $X$ coordinates. By [lem-weil-pbc-glue-schemes] these data give a scheme $Y$ covered by open immersions $V_i\to Y$ whose distinct intersections are exactly $X$. The maps $V_i\to T$ agree on those intersections, so [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] gives $Y\to T$. Its generic fibre is the gluing of copies of $X$ by their entire identity overlaps, hence is $X$; its special fibre has disjoint open charts $(V_i)_k$ and is their coproduct. This proves all claimed chart and fibre identifications.

source.place: Tags 01JB (lemma-glue), 01JC (lemma-glue-schemes); BLR 4.3 Proposition 4, printed p.107, gluing all models along their generic fibres.

proof.text: Restricting the smooth charts of $M_i/T$ to $V_i$ gives smooth charts there, directly from the affine-local definition [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. The covering $Y=\bigcup_i V_i$ and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-on-source] imply that $Y/T$ is smooth. Each $V_i$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Restricting the finite-type affine charts of $M_i$ to $V_i$, then using quasi-compactness to choose a finite subcover, gives a finite cover of $V_i$ by finite-type affine $R$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. There are finitely many $i$, so their combined finite affine cover proves $Y/T$ finite type by that same definition.

source.place: Tag 01V6 (lemma-smooth-characterize), Tag 01T0 (section-finite-type); properties.tex Tags 01OW and 01OZ, Noetherian open subspaces.

proof.text: The products $V_i\times_T V_j$ cover $Y\times_T Y$. On an unmixed product the diagonal is the diagonal of $V_i/T$, a closed immersion because it is the restriction of the diagonal of $M_i/T$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. On a mixed product its inverse image is the overlap $X$, and the diagonal is the closed immersion of Step 8. These local closed immersions imply that the whole diagonal is a closed immersion: its image has closed intersection with every open product in this cover, hence is closed; the local homeomorphisms onto that image glue to a homeomorphism, and surjectivity of the structure-sheaf map holds on the cover, hence globally. These are precisely the two conditions of [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Therefore $Y/T$ is separated. The separation check uses both diagonal and mixed products, and so also applies when $r=1$.

BLR 4.3 Prop 4 is not in literature/. The Q54 maintainer read pp.106-107 and matched the statement; this proof follows BLR's cross-diagonal domination argument, with the forbidden rational map taking the place of minimality. I checked Stacks 09NH (varieties.tex:8913): its hypotheses match the lem-trf node exactly. Checks by step. Steps 1-2: A_i is a DVR via 0HA1, flat torsion-freeness and 00PD. Steps 3-4: Gamma is reduced (056B) and restricts to delta(X) on the generic fibre (restrict-open lemma); the integral neighbourhood from 0BX3 gives a local inclusion A_i in B inside Frac A_i. Step 5: domination forces B=A_i; 09NH plus morphism gluing then gives a base-dense rational identity map, which is a contradiction. Step 6: all hypotheses of the Chevalley node hold. Step 7: a constructible set omitting the generic point has proper closure; this is elementary. Step 8: the closed immersion X into V_i x V_j follows by base change along the open. Steps 9-11: the glue data and cocycle are correct, smoothness and finite type follow from qc Noetherian opens, and separatedness from local closed immersions on the product cover. Edge cases checked: r=1, disconnected X, empty C_ij, any DVR. Quasi-separatedness of delta in Step 3 is left implicit but is elementary.
